clue.text: Song of Frenchman who holds 'e's little and not so hot

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so the Frenchman wraps round what follows

parts.note: homme is French for man
a Cockney 'e's (he is) plus wee, Scottish and everyday British for little

indicators.note: the word hot is not left as it stands, so its letters come in a different order

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A Frenchman, a little fellow, sings a song while not feeling his best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'e's is Cockney for he is, and wee is Scots and everyday British for little; the Frenchman's word is split open to take them.
explanation.definitionFit: Home Sweet Home is a famous nineteenth-century ballad, so it is an example of a song.

clue.text: Immediately beyond control

definitions.meaning: first meaning: at once, without thinking it over
second meaning: no longer manageable, as of an unruly crowd

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it suggests something that suddenly escapes control; it is two separate meanings of one idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both dismissed at once without consideration and unruly, past all management.

clue.text: Muse of a liberator

indicators.note: of here means forming part of, so the letters sit inside the following word

parts.note: the letters run consecutively in the middle of this word

explanation.surface: A poet's inspiring Muse is cast as someone who sets people free.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the one presiding over love poetry.

clue.text: Parliament keeps it within the pale

indicators.note: something that keeps another thing holds it inside, so one word is placed within another

parts.note: wan means pale in complexion
taken as written

explanation.surface: A legislature keeps its business strictly inside acceptable bounds, within the pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Within the pale' looks like the idiom for acceptable conduct; here the pale is just a colour word.
explanation.definitionFit: The witan was the Anglo-Saxon king's council of wise men, an early English national assembly.

clue.text: English prizes surround a good guy going for ninety degrees

definitions.note: an adverb of direction described by its compass bearing

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English

indicators.note: to surround is to enclose on all sides, so the prizes go round the good guy

parts.note: awards are prizes
a saint, abbreviated ST, is a good person

explanation.surface: English prizes are heaped upon a decent fellow at some ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: East lies at a bearing of ninety degrees on the compass, so heading that way is travelling towards it.

clue.text: Ted with time spent in prison has a grouse

parts.note: Ted Heath was British Conservative prime minister 1970-74
bird is British slang for a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A man called Ted, after a spell behind bars, has a complaint to air.
explanation.walkthrough: A grouse looks like a grievance from a jailed man; it is the game bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The heathbird is a name for the black grouse, a moorland game bird of northern Britain.

clue.text: Physical exercise for some sons and some daughters

indicators.note: some sons and some daughters suggests taking only part of something, so a portion of the following words is wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between these two words

explanation.surface: A fitness class is suitable for boys and girls alike.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'some' disguises the instruction: the end of the second 'some' and the start of 'daughters' supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Medau is a system of rhythmic gymnastics developed in Germany by Hinrich Medau and taught widely as keep-fit.

clue.text: Setter in French capital played joker before setter wrote of trio on the Thames

definitions.text: wrote of trio on the Thames
definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the writer who did so

parts.note: the setter is I, which in French is je

indicators.note: something played is performed in a new way, so these letters are worked into a fresh order

parts.note: Rome is a capital city; French belongs with the previous word
taken as written before rearranging
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A setter in Paris plays the fool before another setter writes about three men boating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter in French' gives JE, not a dog; 'French capital' wants to be Paris, but only 'capital' is needed for ROME.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerome K Jerome wrote Three Men in a Boat, the comic tale of three friends rowing up the Thames.

clue.text: Brown painter's passage with writer

parts.note: the Pre-Raphaelite painter Ford Madox Brown's first two names
a ford is a shallow passage across a river

explanation.surface: A painter's passage of brushwork is paired with a writer's prose.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown is not a colour but the painter's surname; his forenames are what the clue takes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ford Madox Ford, grandson of the painter, was the English novelist of The Good Soldier and Parade's End.

clue.text: Piece of former pamphlet

parts.note: ex means former
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious

explanation.surface: Someone quotes a bit of an old leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a passage taken from a longer text, so it is a portion or excerpt of it.

clue.text: Unfinished Georgian architect gets military award, the blighter!

indicators.note: unfinished means the architect's name stops short of its final letter

parts.note: Sir John Soane designed the Bank of England in the Georgian era
DSO is the Distinguished Service Order, a British military decoration

explanation.surface: An architect leaves his building half-done yet still receives a medal, the rascal.
explanation.definitionFit: So-and-so is a mild euphemistic insult for an annoying person, the same as calling someone a blighter.

clue.text: Gluck's work shows goldfish need oxygen

parts.note: the orfe is a fish whose golden variety is kept in ornamental ponds
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A composer's piece illustrates that pet fish must have air to breathe.
explanation.definitionFit: Orfeo ed Euridice is Gluck's best-known opera, retelling the Orpheus myth.

clue.text: From sundown he could work on the Sun

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the kind of person who does

indicators.note: made from signals that the following letters are the raw material for a new word

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A man toils after dark, perhaps a shift worker on a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, not the star.
explanation.definitionFit: A newshound is an eager reporter, the sort of journalist employed by a tabloid paper.

clue.text: Ungulate from oriental country

parts.note: E for East, so oriental
a land is a country

explanation.surface: A hoofed beast comes from somewhere in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope, and antelopes are hoofed mammals.

clue.text: Money changing no sin? That's one way of looking at it

definitions.text: one way of looking at it

parts.note: a dime is a US ten-cent coin

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the letters of the next words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone argues that exchanging currency is no sin, which is one viewpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimension is an aspect or angle of a problem, a particular perspective from which it can be viewed.

clue.text: Wheels, four in number, with big guns for predators

parts.note: wheels is slang for a car

indicators.note: in places one item inside another, so the four sits inside the number

parts.note: NO is the abbreviation for number
IV is four in Roman numerals
RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's big guns

explanation.surface: A four-wheeled armoured vehicle, heavily gunned, is built to hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnivora is the zoological order of flesh-eating mammals such as cats, dogs and bears.

clue.text: Flower for the (say) sinner and the song

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the next word, keeping its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: the spoken word is spelt differently here
an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: A bouquet is offered for a repentant sinner and accompanied by a hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: Cineraria is a daisy-like flowering plant often grown as a pot plant.

clue.text: Tenor goes astray: would this make him a contralto?

definitions.text: would this make him a contralto?
definitions.note: a cryptic description rather than a plain noun

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters stray from their order

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
the word itself joins the fodder as well as signalling the shuffle

explanation.surface: A tenor sings off-key, and the question is whether that drops him into a woman's range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes' is both fodder and part of the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Oestrogen is the main female sex hormone; dosing a man with it might feminise him, perhaps even his voice.

clue.text: Case-law derives from a lot of combat with detectives and models

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is left off

parts.note: judo is a form of unarmed combat
G-men are FBI agents
Model Ts, the old Ford cars

explanation.surface: Legal precedent is drawn from fighting, police work and fashion models.
explanation.definitionFit: Case law is the body of law built up from courts' past rulings on individual cases.

clue.text: Find very short party

indicators.note: very short means heavily cut, so much of the word for find is lopped from the end

parts.note: to discover is to find

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a brief gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Three letters, not one, come off the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a dance party with recorded pop music.

clue.text: Score of 2 to go on for a long time

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket, batsmen scoring one run and then another make two

definitions.text: to go on for a long time
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to keep running, as a long-lived show does

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a run is a single point scored by running between the wickets.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used of a long-lasting play or story that continues for years, and literally of two runs scored.

clue.text: The tree on the Marsh in North Georgia before 10

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for North
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
10 drawn as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A lone tree stands on swampland somewhere in the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marsh is the crime writer Ngaio Marsh, whose first name is a New Zealand tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The ngaio is a small New Zealand coastal tree, and it was also the first name of novelist Ngaio Marsh.

clue.text: Nymph close to poster, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: nigh means close, and an ad is a poster

explanation.surface: A water spirit lingers by a billboard, or so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A naiad is a water nymph of Greek myth, living in rivers and springs.

clue.text: Backfires

definitions.note: the whole clue is a cryptic hint: the word read back is the answer, which is not otherwise defined

indicators.note: back tells us to read the rest of the word from the end to the start

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue looks like one verb about engines; split it and the second half is to be read back. There is no separate definition beyond the clue itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small finishing stroke on printed letters, which the reversed word happens to spell.

clue.text: Battle for badger's home circle

parts.note: a sett is a badger's burrow
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: Animals fight over a badger's territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is an informal word for a fight or heated argument.

clue.text: More substantial job in France with advanced entry

indicators.note: with here means having inside, so one letter is taken into the job word

parts.note: métier is the French word for trade or job
A is the abbreviation for advanced

explanation.surface: A bigger job awaits in France for someone with an advanced qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: Meatier is the comparative of meaty, which figuratively means having lots of substance or content.

clue.text: Whole number, say, in Bury

indicators.note: in places the example inside the word for burying

parts.note: to inter is to bury
e.g. means for example, as say does

explanation.surface: A figure is quoted for the town of Bury in Lancashire.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury, with its capital, looks like the English town; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a number with no fractional part, a whole number in arithmetic.

clue.text: Bit of a fight with a bullet doesn''t seem to be getting anywhere

definitions.text: doesn''t seem to be getting anywhere

parts.note: a round is one stage of a boxing match
and means together with
a round is a single cartridge of ammunition

explanation.surface: A gunfight in the boxing ring goes nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Going round and round means circling endlessly without progress, as in an unproductive discussion.
